params.body:
The first round on real names showed the rule up immediately. `gentells` and `signal-observatory-gentells` send through Resend and receive at `inbound-smtp.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com`. That MX belongs to none of the recognised senders, so the scan offered no SPF line at all — while the line it could have offered (`v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all`) is right. Mail that **arrives** at a foreign name says nothing about whether that name also **sends**.

So the draft now comes with the doubt beside it (`spfDraftCaveat`): where the mail arrives, that we do not know that name as a sender, and what to do if it does send. Whoever runs the domain knows that, and they are the one reading the line; we cannot see it from outside and no longer pretend either way.

kubo-it-lab and she-cosmetics came out clean and correct in that same round (`include:_spf.google.com include:servers.mcsv.net ~all`, `include:spf.protection.outlook.com ~all`), so the drafts themselves hold.

665 tests, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: Twijfel naast het voorstel, in plaats van zwijgen
